title: Why Asian Parents REALLY Want You to Be a Doctor
description: Doctor, lawyer, or disappointment. Sound familiar? But the reason behind it is actually way deeper than you think. What did YOUR parents want you to be? Comment below!

sections.narration: Imagine you tell your Asian parents you want to be an artist, and they just stare.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy holding paintbrush, two parents staring blankly, warm room

sections.narration: Then your mom says, 'That's nice, but have you considered medical school?'
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy with paint palette, woman holding medical textbook, warm

sections.narration: And your dad quietly slides a law school brochure across the dinner table.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy at dinner table, man sliding paper, warm kitchen light

sections.narration: So here's the real story — many Asian families came from really tough circumstances.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy looking at old family photo, sepia warm tones

sections.narration: Your grandparents probably worked incredibly hard just to keep the family stable.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy beside elderly couple in work clothes, golden hour light

sections.narration: And it gets deeper — in many Asian cultures, your success reflects on your whole family.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy on podium, family portraits connected by lines, warm tones

sections.narration: But here's the thing — it's not about controlling you, it's about protecting you.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy under umbrella held by parent figure, warm rainy scene

sections.narration: They want careers where you'll always have stability, no matter what happens.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy standing on solid ground, shaky ground around, warm colors

sections.narration: So THAT'S why 'doctor or lawyer' isn't about prestige — it's about security.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy with lightbulb, stethoscope and briefcase floating, warm

sections.narration: Every time they push you, they're really saying 'I don't want you to struggle.'
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy and parent figure, warm embrace silhouette, golden light

sections.narration: Next time they mention med school, you'll understand what they actually mean.
sections.visual_notes: Centered: boy smiling at parent, warm family dinner scene, soft glow
Centered: boy giving thumbs up, warm earth-toned background, simple
